details.formulaDescription: Parse start and target finish as minutes since midnight; require start < target finish, otherwise an order error. crewLeadMinutes defaults to 20 and must be between 0 and 120. Access points must be at least one, with strictly increasing km between 0 and distanceKm and a non-empty name. Pace = distanceKm / (target - start) km per minute. For each point, arrival = start + km / pace; crew call clock = arrival - crewLeadMinutes. A point with crew true or pacer true appears in handoffs; a point with both false appears only in warnings. Pacer legs are the segments between consecutive pacer-true points, with km equal to the distance between them. Crew gaps are adjacent arrival differences among crew-true points; longestCrewGapMinutes is the largest, rounded to the nearest minute (0 when fewer than two crew points). A crew gap above 120 minutes and any neither-crew-nor-pacer point produce a warning; a single crew point also produces a warning that gaps cannot be checked.
assumptions: Arrival projections assume an even pace from start to target finish; climbs, stops and fatigue are not modelled.
All clocks are on the same day; cross-midnight arrival is not handled.
Crew and pacer rights shown per point come from the race's official access list; the tool does not verify them against current regulations.
The 120-minute long-gap threshold is a planning heuristic, not an official rule.
The planner schedules where crew and pacers can appear, not how supplies, transport or communication are arranged on site.
details.rounding: Arrival and call clocks round to the nearest whole minute; crew gaps and longest gap round to the nearest whole minute; pacer leg km keep two decimals.
